title: [Bug]: GTP-U Error Indication on S5-U tears down the whole IMS PDN without notifying the MME (VoLTE UE stuck until re-attach)

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

The EPC Error Indication branch does not distinguish dedicated vs. default
bearers and never notifies the MME. TS 23.007 only mentions local cleanup
(“may notify O&M”), but a silent local delete of the default bearer leaves
the MME/UE desynchronised, which is the stuck‑UE symptom above.

EPC (S/P-GW split, CUPS) with an IMS APN used for VoLTE:

```
MME  ── S11 ──  SGW-C ── S5-C ──  SMF/PGW-C
                  │                   │
               (SGW-U) ── S5-U ── (UPF / PGW-U, IMS APN)
                  │
                S1-U ── eNB(s)
```

1. A VoLTE-capable UE attaches and establishes the IMS PDN connection
   (default bearer + a dedicated QCI‑1 bearer while on a call).
2. Place a VoLTE call so the UE is `ECM-CONNECTED` with active bearers.
3. Trigger a rapid / ping‑pong X2 (or S1) handover between two eNBs during
   the call. The SGW‑U downlink path‑switch (new eNB S1‑U F‑TEID) races with
   in‑flight downlink IMS media, so the PGW‑U forwards a downlink G‑PDU to a
   SGW‑U S5‑U F‑TEID that is momentarily stale.
4. The SGW‑U replies with a **GTP‑U Error Indication** on S5‑U for that
   F‑TEID; the PGW‑U reports it to the SMF as a PFCP Session Report
   (Error Indication Report).

The Error Indication can also be injected directly against the PGW‑U's S5‑U
downlink F‑TEID to reproduce deterministically (single crafted GTP‑U
Error Indication packet), without needing to provoke the handover race.



### Logs

```shell
[smf] ERROR: [imsi:...] Error Indication from SGW-C (n4-handler.c)
[smf] ERROR: EPC Session Released by Error Indication (gsm.c)


After this, the SMF/UPF PFCP session for the IMS PDN is gone, but **no**
`Delete Bearer Request` is sent to the MME, so there is no NAS
`Deactivate EPS Bearer Context Request` / detach toward the UE.
```

### Expected behaviour

Per **3GPP TS 23.007** (handling of a GTP‑U Error Indication at the P‑GW):

- Error Indication for a **dedicated** bearer → delete **only that bearer**.
- Error Indication for the **default** bearer → delete **all bearers of the
  PDN connection**.

In either case the P‑GW/SMF should run the PGW‑initiated bearer deactivation
procedure (Delete Bearer Request → SGW → MME → NAS deactivation toward the
UE) so that SGW / MME / UE stay synchronised and the UE can re‑establish the
IMS PDN and continue placing / receiving VoLTE calls.



### Observed Behaviour

`smf_n4_handle_session_report_request()` (EPC branch, `src/smf/n4-handler.c`)
calls `smf_epc_pfcp_send_session_deletion_request(sess, OGS_INVALID_POOL_ID)`
for **any** Error Indication, regardless of which bearer the reported F‑TEID
belongs to. This has two problems:

1. **Over‑deletion.** The whole PFCP session is torn down via the GSM FSM
   (`EPC Session Released by Error Indication` →
   `smf_gsm_state_session_will_release` → `smf_sess_remove()`), even when the
   Error Indication is for a single **dedicated** (voice) bearer. TS 23.007
   requires only that dedicated bearer to be removed in that case.
2. **No MME/UE notification.** No `Delete Bearer Request` is sent to the MME.
   The MME and UE keep a ghost IMS PDN connection. Data on other APNs keeps
   working, but the UE is unaware the IMS PDN is gone and **cannot originate a
   new VoLTE call until it re‑attaches** (e.g. airplane‑mode toggle).

Net effect: a single transient, handover‑induced Error Indication
permanently breaks VoLTE for that UE until a manual re‑attach.



### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_
